title: Kiosk schema descriptor
description: The body of the unauthenticated GET <endpoint>/schema: the origin's verbs and their contracts. The root is CLOSED. The module set is in `capabilities` in /.well-known/kiosk.json.

events.description: Topic descriptors, sorted by name. An origin that serves no topics answers [], exactly as one with no actions answers []: a member that appears only sometimes is a member every reader has to branch on, and whether the module is served at all is stated once, in `capabilities`.

descriptor.description: One verb's description. CLOSED (Section 8.3): a descriptor carries the members named here and no others. An operator that needs another member proposes it for the protocol.

name.description: The verb's name, which is also its path segment under `endpoint`. One name is one KIND: a name listed under `queries` must not also appear under `actions`.

description.description: Human-facing description or null. SEMANTICS live here in prose -- what the verb does, when to reach for it, what the result means. Names, types and constraints do not: an input belongs to input_schema and a result field to output_schema.

reach.description: Whose rows this verb may touch (Section 7.2). `principal`, the default: the caller's own rows and rows that belong to no principal. `published`: rows the operator shows to every principal. `consented`: rows a principal shared. `role`: rows the caller's operator-assigned role reaches. An AI assistant MUST read a missing `reach` as `principal`.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for this verb's inputs, and the only place a parameter is declared. The operator validates the arguments against it and answers 400 bad_request otherwise. A verb that takes nothing declares the closed empty object.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for what this verb returns. A query's is an array schema, also when it paginates: the cursor is in an RFC 8288 Link header. A success body that does not satisfy it is an operator defect.

params.description: FORBIDDEN. `false` refuses the key outright; `null` is a value too (Section 8.3). A verb declares its inputs in `input_schema`.

example_params.description: Example params object an AI assistant can copy verbatim as a starting call for this verb. It ILLUSTRATES input_schema and is not the contract: where the two disagree, the schema is right.

example_row.description: Example of one result element -- a representative row for a query, or the example return value for an action. It ILLUSTRATES output_schema and is not the contract.

topic.description: One event topic this origin publishes. CLOSED, as a verb descriptor is.

name.description: The topic name, drawn from the same vocabulary as a verb name.

description.description: Prose semantics, on the same terms as a verb's.

reach.description: Whose events a subscriber may read. The same four values, with the same meanings, as a verb's reach.

payload_schema.description: JSON Schema for the event's `data`. It is declared for the reason a verb's output_schema is: without it a message cannot be consumed without receiving one and observing what arrived.

examples.description: Example `data` objects, each satisfying payload_schema. They ILLUSTRATE payload_schema and are not the contract: where the two disagree, the schema is right.
